newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Chronology of recent events in war-battered Angola.
newsitem.headline: Chronology of recent events in war-battered Angola.

text.p: The Angolan government and its former rebel UNITA foes were scheduled to form a power-sharing government on Friday.
Following is a chronology of key events in Angola's recent history.

1975 - Left-wing revolution in Portugal spells end of Lisbon's African empire. In Angola three main guerrilla groups share power: Jonas Savimbi's National Union for the Total Independence of Angola (UNITA), the Marxist Popular Movement for the Liberation of Angola (MPLA) and the National Liberation Front of Angola (FNLA).
1976 - MPLA crushes FNLA and drives back UNITA.
1979 - MPLA leader Agostinho Neto dies, replaced by Soviet-trained Jose Eduardo dos Santos.
1987 - South African force enters southeast Angola to thwart MPLA and Cuban offensive against UNITA.
1988 - South Africans withdraw.
1989 - At African summit in Zaire dos Santos and Savimbi agree on ceasefire, which collapses in August.
April - MPLA ditches Marxism-Leninism for social democracy and starts preparing for general elections.
May - Dos Santos, Savimbi sign peace accord in Lisbon.
Sept - Angolans vote in first multiparty U.N.-monitored polls for president and 223-seat national assembly.

Oct - UNITA withdraws from the newly unified armed forces accusing government of election fraud. MPLA wins 53.7 percent and UNITA 34.1 percent of national assembly vote. Dos Santos takes 49.57 percent and Savimbi 40.07 percent of presidential vote, forcing second round. U.N. certifies poll as generally free and fair.
Oct-Nov - Fighting flares, more than 300 people killed in Luanda as UNITA refuses to accept election results.
1993 - U.N.-arranged peace talks open in Lusaka, Zambia.
Nov - Angolan government and UNITA sign Lusaka Protocol peace accord.
Feb - U.N. announces deployment of 7,000 peacekeepers.
May - Dos Santos and Savimbi hold peace summit in Lusaka, reiterate commitment to peace accord.
Sept - First peacekeepers arrive.
March - Savimbi, dos Santos agree to form unity government and to merge forces into a new national army by July.
March 22 - Savimbi announces he will be head of the largest opposition party, and not take a unity government post.
April 11 - Formation of new government of national unity, but Savimbi declines to attend inauguation ceremony in Luanda.
